gen-eater-fs-familjen-grotesk: Dark and a little aggressive, Eater has the worn look of a wooden stamp, its thin and heavy strokes only mildly apart. And Familjen Grotesk is the lively sans underneath, tall in the lowercase and a bit unfinished in its bowls.
gen-gf-paprika-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its curves apart and its line the same width from start to finish. Paprika, the heading, is the showier one, with lowercase that fills the line like capitals while Work Sans simply stays tidy.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-synonym: Synonym is a plain sans with wide-open curves. Phudu, the heading, brings bold, distinctive letters with the same generous terminals, and that shared openness is what ties them together.
gen-gf-phudu-space-grotesk: Bold and distinctive, Phudu opens its curves wide and draws them with a ballpoint's pressure-free line. And Space Grotesk, a plain sans, would carry a long passage in a geometric ribbon of constant width, steady and quietly neutral.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-amulya: Amulya reads modern and unfussy, its curves staying generous. Pixelify Sans heads the pair with a steady line that never shifts pressure, so a long stretch of Amulya feels like an easy, open sequence of shapes beside it.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-plein: Neon glass, bent into letters. Pixelify Sans does that tube-like, expressive heading work best, while Plein, a plain sans, does the clean, reliable job with a clear channel leading into each round letter.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-spline-sans: Chunky, bold, a bit playful. Spline Sans, a plain sans, then lays down wide gaps and strokes of identical weight beneath Pixelify Sans, so its steady heading line gets an approachable, contemporary partner.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-synonym: Bold and blocky, with a paperclip-open c. Synonym, a plain sans, then runs along in a dependable stripe of constant ink, so Pixelify Sans above it keeps all the attitude and the text stays clean.
gen-irish-grover-switzer: Irish Grover has tall lowercase that makes every word look sturdy and large, with softly varied strokes and open throats. Switzer, a plain sans, runs thin and tubular beneath it.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-fs-amulya: Shantell Sans has a wide, open mouth and one fixed nib width, giving it a distinctive hand-drawn feel. Amulya handles the modern, generous-curved text.
